chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Abde Rabb al-Ansari al-Hamadani, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Hashmi, from the descendants of Abbas, said:

I attended the house of Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) in Sarmanra on the day he passed away. His coffin was brought out and placed outside, and we were thirty-nine men sitting, waiting. Then a boy, ten years old in height, came out to us, barefoot, with his cloak over his shoulder and face. When he came out, we stood up out of awe for him, without knowing him. He advanced, and the people stood up and formed rows behind him. He led the funeral prayer and walked, then entered a room other than the one he had come out of. Abu Abdullah al-Hamadani said: 'I met a man from Tabriz in Maragha known as Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Tabrizi, and he narrated to me the same report of al-Hashmi without omitting anything.' I asked al-Hamadani: 'Was the boy ten years old in height or in age?' For it was narrated that the birth was in the year 258 AH, and the occultation of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) was in the year 260 AH, four years after the birth. He said: 'I do not know. I heard it thus.' A scholar with good understanding from his town, who had narrations and knowledge, said to me: 'Ten years old in height.'
ai.seo_question: What was the physical stature of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) when he emerged after his father's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a crucial eyewitness account of the transition from the death of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) to the emergence of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.), highlighting the physical presence of the young Imam during the funeral prayers. The narrative underscores the scholarly debate regarding the Imam's age at the time of his emergence, with the consensus leaning towards him being ten years old in height ('ashari al-qad'), which helps reconcile the timeline of his birth and the onset of the Minor Ghayba. This event serves as a foundational proof for the continuity of the Imamate and the reality of the Hidden Imam's physical existence among the people.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 226 - It is narrated from Ahmad bin Ali Raazi from Muhammad bin Ali from Muhammad bin Abde Rabb Ansari Hamadani from Ahmad bin Abdullah Hashmi, a descendant of Abbas that he said:

“One day in Sarmanra, when His Eminence, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) passed away, I went to his house. When his coffin was brought out of his chamber and placed outside, we were thirty-nine persons who had come to attend the funeral. Just then a child, who apparently seemed to be ten years old, came out with a sheet on his shoulder and face. As soon as he entered, awe struck us, so that we rose up to welcome him. He stood up and all of us stood behind him. He recited the funeral prayers and then went away. But he did not go back into the room from which he had emerged; he went into another room.” Abu Abdullah Hamadani says: “I met Ibrahim bin Muhammad Tabrizi in Maragha and he also narrated to me the above report of Ahmad bin Abdullah Hashmi verbatim.”
